jurisdiction.name: Croatia
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Croatia has no dedicated AI law or adopted AI strategy yet: AI policy sits in the Digital Croatia Strategy 2032, and in May 2025 the government launched work on a National AI Development Plan to 2032 with a 2026-2028 action plan, which was still being drafted in October 2026. No act implementing the EU AI Act or designating its authorities has been published. The data protection authority (AZOP) is the most active issuer of AI guidance, with 2025-2026 guidance for AI developers, on large language models and on automated decisions, and the State School for Public Administration surveyed state bodies' AI readiness in 2025.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Justice, Public Administration and Digital Transformation
narrative.review_notes: This review was completed on 12 October 2026 and covers national law, government, ministries and regulators. Croatia's national AI plan and its law implementing the EU AI Act are still being drafted and are listed as leads.

instruments.official_title: Strategija digitalne Hrvatske za razdoblje do 2032. godine
instruments.english_title: Digital Croatia Strategy for the period until 2032
instruments.current_status: In force as Croatia's overarching digital strategy (NN 2/2023). AI-specific policy is to be set out in the National AI Development Plan to 2032, which was still being drafted in October 2026 (see leads).
instruments.summary: Croatia's national digital strategy to 2032, adopted by the Croatian Parliament on 16 December 2022 and published in Narodne novine 2/2023. It has four priority areas (digital transition of the economy, digitalisation of public administration, broadband networks, digital skills) and names AI among the advanced technologies to be adopted by businesses and public administration, including monitoring good practice in public-sector AI use, AI-enabled open-data and analytics platforms, and adapting laws and by-laws needed to enable AI use. It also calls for legislation on new technologies such as AI to be assessed for impact on innovation.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Overarching digital strategy with an AI pillar for the economy and public administration, pending the dedicated National AI Development Plan.

instruments.current_status: Adopted at the 87th Government session on 2 May 2025 (session material and MPUDT news of 2 May 2025); no Narodne novine publication was located. The expert working group first met on 27 May 2025; the plan itself had not been published or adopted by 12 October 2026 (see leads).
instruments.summary: Government decision under the Act on the Strategic Planning System tasking the Ministry of Justice, Public Administration and Digital Transformation with drafting a National AI Development Plan to 2032 and a first Action Plan for 2026-2028. The plan is to frame public policy and investment in AI and the conditions for its effective use across society and the economy, with attention to safe and ethical use; the minister must appoint an expert working group within 30 days and inform the public of the start of drafting within 8 days. The explanatory note lists education and skills, digitalisation, economic growth, research and start-up incentives, and protection of citizens' rights and privacy as key aspects.

instruments.official_title: Zakon o provedbi Opće uredbe o zaštiti podataka
instruments.english_title: Act on the Implementation of the General Data Protection Regulation
instruments.current_status: Published in Narodne novine NN 42/2018 on 9 May 2018 and in force since 25 May 2018 (art. 57).
instruments.summary: National act implementing the GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679) in Croatia, published in Narodne novine 42/2018. It establishes the Personal Data Protection Agency (AZOP) as the supervisory authority and sets national rules, including on processing biometric data in the public and private sectors, video surveillance and data of children. It governs the personal-data processing involved in training and using AI systems in Croatia.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Data protection law under which AZOP supervises AI-related processing of personal data.

instruments.official_title: Zaštita osobnih podataka i umjetna inteligencija: često postavljana pitanja
instruments.english_title: Personal Data Protection and Artificial Intelligence: Frequently Asked Questions
instruments.current_status: Published on AZOP's 'Umjetna inteligencija i zaštita osobnih podataka' page, which dates it 20.8.2025; the PDF itself is undated.
instruments.summary: AZOP's 39-page FAQ on the interplay between the GDPR and the EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689). It explains why AI is regulated, the AI Act's phased application, and how data protection principles, legal bases, data subject rights and impact assessments apply when personal data are processed by AI systems. It is addressed to controllers, processors and the public.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: First consolidated AI guidance from Croatia's data protection authority.

instruments.official_title: Zaštita podataka i umjetna inteligencija: Smjernice za subjekte koji razvijaju modele i sustave umjetne inteligencije
instruments.english_title: Data Protection and Artificial Intelligence: Guidelines for entities developing AI models and systems
instruments.current_status: Published 7 May 2026 (AZOP news item 'Objavljene nove smjernice...').
instruments.summary: AZOP's 87-page guidance for organisations that develop, train, test, integrate or use AI systems. It covers when the GDPR applies to AI models (models trained on personal data are not automatically anonymous), how to allocate controller/processor roles between providers and deployers, purpose definition, legal bases including the legitimate-interest test and limits on scraping public data, data protection by design, transparency, data subject rights, DPIAs and security risks such as attacks on models and LLM-specific risks.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Main practical AI compliance guidance from Croatia's data protection regulator.

instruments.official_title: Preporuka za sigurno korištenje velikih jezičnih modela i sustava temeljenih na velikim jezičnim modelima (Large Language Models-LLMs)
instruments.english_title: Recommendation on the safe use of large language models and LLM-based systems
instruments.current_status: Published 8 May 2026; listed among AZOP's recommendations (Preporuke).
instruments.summary: AZOP recommendation, issued under Article 57(1) GDPR, on using public chatbots and other generative AI tools based on large language models. It advises users and organisations not to enter personal data, data about others, confidential or internal documents, official files or health, financial or employment data into LLM systems unless the tool's use has been assessed, has a legal basis and is organisationally controlled, because input can trigger new processing by external providers (storage, access, model training).
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Regulator's generative AI usage recommendation for organisations and individuals.

instruments.official_title: Preporuka o primjeni članka 22. Opće uredbe o zaštiti podataka u kontekstu automatiziranog donošenja odluka, profiliranja i uporabe sustava umjetne inteligencije
instruments.english_title: Recommendation on the application of Article 22 GDPR to automated decision-making, profiling and the use of AI systems
instruments.current_status: Published 11 May 2026; listed among AZOP's recommendations (Preporuke).
instruments.summary: AZOP recommendation clarifying controllers' obligations when algorithmic, machine-learning, scoring, ranking or risk-assessment systems support decisions about individuals. It sets a three-question test (is there a decision, does it have legal or similarly significant effects, is there real rather than formal human involvement), stresses that labelling output as a 'recommendation' or 'score' does not avoid Article 22 (citing CJEU SCHUFA, C-634/21), and calls for understandable transparency about how algorithms and AI affect decisions.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Regulator guidance on automated decision-making by AI systems.

instruments.current_status: Report dated November 2025 on its cover; the PDF was uploaded to the DŠJU site in early 2026.
instruments.summary: Report by the State School for Public Administration presenting an 'AI index' of Croatian state administration bodies based on a survey of their readiness to introduce AI and their training needs. It finds pioneers and motivated staff with management support, but gaps in digital and analytical skills, infrastructure, internal rules, procedures and ethical standards for AI use and in system-level strategic direction, and makes recommendations including targeted training.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: National sources in Croatia were searched, including the official gazette, government session materials, the consultation portal, ministries and regulators. No qualifying material was found for ethics, procurement, cyber-security, standards, sandboxes, sectoral rules, drafts, international instruments or historical documents; the national law implementing the EU AI Act and the National AI Development Plan are still being prepared. Not yet verified from the official text: the standards institute catalogue and the parliamentary bill tracker, which were searched only indirectly, and whether authorities under the EU AI Act have been designated.
coverage_audit.technical_note: Coverage note (original): Technical review notes: tier B/C batch run 2026-10-12, one agent, national level only (PROTOCOL §6), about 25-minute time box. Narodne novine search ignored URL parameters (targeted searches and direct article URLs used). HZN catalogue and the Sabor bill tracker not searched directly. Not recorded: AZOP's unofficial translation of an EDPB report, the OECD NCP translation, and the July 2026 AI factory funding decision. Convention 108: NN Međunarodni ugovori 4/2005, item 38, recorded on the COE file. Units covered: Law: Narodne novine (Digital Croatia Strategy NN 2/2023, GDPR Implementation Act NN 42/2018, Convention 108 ratification NN MU 4/2005); searched for an AI Act implementing act, AI bills and AI provisions in other laws: none found (national AI Act implementing law still being drafted, held as lead). The gazette's own search could not be driven by URL, so gazette coverage relied on targeted searches.; Government: Government session materials (2 May 2025 decision launching the National AI Development Plan); Digital Croatia Strategy 2032; National AI Development Plan not yet published (lead); e-Savjetovanja searched, no AI consultation found.; Ministries: MPUDT (digital ministry, AI plan and AI Act working group); State School for Public Administration (AI index); education (MZOM), economy (MINGO, OECD NCP translation of OECD AI due-diligence guidance only), health, defence, finance, labour and interior searched: no ministry-issued AI guidance found.; Regulators: AZOP (FAQ 2025, developer guidelines, LLM and Article 22 recommendations 2026); HNB, HANFA, HAKOM and the Agency for Electronic Media searched: no AI-specific documents found; no AI-related AZOP fine located. National cybersecurity centre searched: no AI guidance found.. Not reached: Croatian Standards Institute (HZN) catalogue not searched directly (only a web search for an HRN adoption of ISO/IEC 42001, nothing found); Sabor bill tracker not searched directly (web searches found no AI bill beyond an MP's 2023/2024 AI resolution proposal the Government recommended rejecting). Could not verify: Whether Croatia has notified AI Act market surveillance/notifying authorities or Article 77 fundamental-rights bodies (no official act found); Ratification of Convention 108+ (CETS 223) in Narodne novine; AZOP 'Rizici u sustavima umjetne inteligencije i mjere za njihovo ublažavanje' is an unofficial Croatian translation of an EDPB Support Pool of Experts report, not recorded as a national instrument. ethics, procurement, cyber-security, standards, sandbox, sectoral, drafts, international, historical: no material found.
